title: A containment figure asks: does the smaller uncertainty region sit inside the larger one, and when do they coincide?
summary: Two ellipses in the plane of two retained parameters: the marginal region (the full uncertainty after ignoring a third parameter) and the conditional region (the uncertainty when that third parameter is fixed). When the removed parameter is correlated with the retained ones, the conditional ellipse is strictly inside; when it is not, they are identical.

media.alt: Two panels of normalized parameter deviations, Delta A over sigma A on x and Delta n over sigma n on y, both from minus 1 to 1. Left, correlated: a solid red tilted ellipse (marginal) contains a smaller dashed blue ellipse (conditional), with the band between them shaded pink. Right, uncorrelated: the red and blue ellipses coincide.

source.caption: Ellipsoid-containment theory figure
source.note: A geometric illustration of how the physically valid region of joint Arrhenius-parameter space is represented and checked for containment — the theoretical figure behind the sampling-validity concept used throughout this line of work.

read_the_figure.question: What happens to the joint uncertainty region of two parameters when a third, correlated parameter is held fixed instead of integrated out?
read_the_figure.axes: x: the deviation of the first retained parameter from its nominal value, in units of its own standard deviation (Delta A over sigma A). y: the same for the second retained parameter (Delta n over sigma n). Both axes run from about minus 1 to 1. Red solid curve: the boundary of the marginal ellipse. Blue dashed curve: the boundary of the conditional ellipse. Shading marks the interior of each. The left panel is the correlated case (the cross-covariance between the retained block and the removed parameter is not zero); the right panel is the uncorrelated case (it is zero). The title states the containment, conditional inside marginal, and which parameters are retained (A and n) and which removed (E_a).
look_at: Left panel: the blue dashed ellipse lies inside the red one and runs along it on the upper-left and lower-right arcs. The pink band between the curves is the part of the uncertainty that disappears by fixing the removed parameter.
Right panel: the two curves coincide exactly (the dashes of one lie on the other). Fixing a parameter that is uncorrelated with the others removes no uncertainty.

The tilt of the ellipses (long axis rising to the right) comes from the correlation between the two retained parameters. It is present in both panels; the zero in 'Sigma 12 equals 0' refers to the retained-versus-removed block, not to the correlation between A and n.
The red ellipse touches 1 on both axes: the axes are in units of standard deviations, so the marginal ellipse spans one standard deviation along each parameter axis.

Estimate the extent of the blue ellipse along each axis (about 0.8 on the horizontal and about 0.85 on the vertical, read by eye). The shortfall below 1 measures how strongly each retained parameter is correlated with the removed one.
read_the_figure.proves: The containment in the title holds when the conditional covariance is the Schur complement of the full covariance: the conditional region is always inside the marginal one and equals it only when the cross-covariance vanishes. The figure is an illustration of that theorem for a two-dimensional slice, not a numerical result about the real parameters.
if_wrong: A blue ellipse that pokes outside the red one: not possible for exact Gaussian conditioning, so it would signal a bug or a different definition (for example fixing the removed parameter at a value other than its nominal).
Two identical ellipses in the correlated case: the cross-covariance is in fact zero, or the same matrix was plotted twice.
Ellipses that do not touch the plot's boundary at 1: the axes were not normalized by the standard deviations used for the covariance.
Reading the ellipse as a probability region without saying which level: the figure uses a fixed level of the quadratic form, not a 95 percent region.
must_check: Both ellipses are drawn at the same level of the quadratic form.
The axes are in normalized units, and the retained and removed parameters are named in the title.
The two panels use the same scale, so the sizes can be compared.
The figure says what is held fixed in the conditional case, and at what value.
The legend distinguishes marginal and conditional by both colour and line style.

terms.meaning: The covariance of the retained parameters when the removed one is averaged over (ignored). It is simply the corresponding block of the full covariance.
The covariance of the retained parameters when the removed one is held fixed. It is the Schur complement of the full matrix.
The set of parameter values whose quadratic form with the inverse covariance is below a chosen level. In two dimensions it is an ellipse.
The normalized covariance between two parameters; it tilts the ellipse.
The matrix A minus B D inverse C built from a block matrix; it is the covariance left over after conditioning.
The pre-exponential factor A, the temperature exponent n and the activation energy E_a of a rate constant k = A T^n exp(-E_a/RT). They are strongly correlated in fitted data.

remember: Conditioning on a correlated variable shrinks uncertainty; conditioning on an uncorrelated one does nothing.
The conditional covariance is the Schur complement: S11 minus S12 S22 inverse S21.
The subtracted term is positive semidefinite, so the conditional ellipse is always inside the marginal one.
The tilt of an ellipse is the correlation between its own two axes.
Normalized axes make the marginal ellipse touch plus and minus one.

understand.title: Why fix a parameter at all
understand.text: A rate constant has three parameters but a model may only be allowed to vary two, with the third held at its nominal value. The question is what uncertainty region is then legitimate to sample: the full marginal one (too generous, since the third is fixed) or the conditional one (tighter, consistent with fixing).

understand.title: Why containment matters
understand.text: Samples drawn from the conditional region are, by the containment, also valid members of the marginal region. A sample cloud that stays inside the smaller ellipse can therefore be called consistent with the larger uncertainty, which is the practical check the figure illustrates.

understand.title: What the second panel is for
understand.text: It is the limiting case that shows the correlation is responsible for the shrinkage: set the cross-covariance to zero and the two ellipses become the same curve.

steps.title: Partition the covariance
steps.note: Block 11 is for the retained parameters, block 22 for the removed one, and 12 holds the cross-covariances.

steps.title: Marginal and conditional covariances
steps.note: Standard results for a jointly Gaussian vector: the marginal is the block itself, and conditioning on the other variables subtracts the explained part.

steps.title: The subtracted term is positive semidefinite
steps.note: Because the full covariance is positive definite, Sigma 22 inverse is positive definite and the product with its transpose-shaped neighbours is positive semidefinite.

steps.title: Order reverses for inverses
steps.note: Inversion reverses the matrix order. So any x with x transposed times the conditional inverse times x at most c also satisfies the marginal inequality.

steps.title: Containment of the ellipses
steps.tex: \mathcal E_{\Sigma_\mathrm{cond}}=\{x:\ x^{\top}\Sigma_\mathrm{cond}^{-1}x\le c\}\ \subseteq\ \{x:\ x^{\top}\Sigma_r^{-1}x\le c\}=\mathcal E_{\Sigma_r}
steps.note: This is the statement in the figure's title. If Sigma 12 is zero the subtracted term vanishes and the two sets are equal, which is the right panel.

steps.title: Shrinkage for a single removed parameter
steps.note: For one retained variable x and one removed variable y the conditional variance is reduced by the factor one minus rho squared. A conditional ellipse that spans 0.8 of the marginal extent along an axis corresponds to rho of about 0.6.

worked.title: Correlation implied by the shrunken ellipse
worked.problem: The blue ellipse's extent along the horizontal axis is about 0.78 of the red one's (read by eye). Treating E_a as the single removed parameter, what correlation between Delta A and E_a does that imply? And what extent would rho = 0.6 give?

worked.answer: About 0.63 (read by eye, approximate), and 0.8 for rho = 0.6. The shortfall of the blue ellipse below 1 is a direct picture of the correlation with the removed parameter.

analyze.q: Why is the right panel still tilted although Sigma 12 is zero?
analyze.hint: Which block does Sigma 12 refer to?

analyze.q: Could the blue ellipse be larger than the red one in some direction if the full matrix is a valid covariance? Prove it cannot.
analyze.hint: Use the positive semidefinite subtracted term.

analyze.q: Fixing E_a at a value other than the nominal shifts the centre of the conditional ellipse. How would the figure change?
analyze.hint: The conditional mean moves with the value of the fixed parameter; the shape does not.

evaluate.q: Which region is appropriate to sample from when E_a is held fixed in the model: marginal or conditional? Why?
evaluate.hint: Consistency with what the model can vary.

evaluate.q: The picture is a two-dimensional slice of a larger space. What can it not show?
evaluate.hint: Interactions with parameters not drawn; non-Gaussian shapes.

create: Draw a three-panel version with correlation 0, 0.5 and 0.9 between the retained and the removed parameter, and mark the extents of the conditional ellipse on each axis.
Overlay samples drawn from the conditional distribution on the figure and add a count of how many fall inside each ellipse.

checks.q: What does the pink band between the curves represent?
checks.answer: The part of the marginal uncertainty that is explained by the removed parameter and so disappears when that parameter is held fixed.

checks.q: A removed parameter is correlated with a retained one at rho = 0.8. By what factor does the conditional standard deviation shrink?
The two ellipses coincide. What can you say about the cross-covariance?
checks.answer: It is zero (the retained and removed parameters are uncorrelated), so conditioning does not change the retained covariance.

checks.q: Is the containment a result about the real rate parameters?
checks.hint: It is a theorem about Gaussians.
checks.answer: No. It is a property of Gaussian covariance matrices. For the real parameters it holds only to the extent that a Gaussian description is adequate.

checks.q: How would you check numerically that sampling from the conditional distribution stays inside the marginal ellipse?
checks.answer: Draw samples, compute x transposed times the marginal inverse covariance times x for each, and check that the fraction with value below c is at least the fraction for the conditional ellipse (they are inside whenever the conditional quadratic form is below c).
